rationale.conceptual: The method is a custom combination of multi-task Gaussian process regression, a specialized inverse-distance covariance function, and the dimer algorithm, applied to DFT calculations. Implementation requires non-trivial understanding of both machine learning (GP, multi-task learning, custom kernels) and computational materials science (ion relaxation, transition state search). This goes beyond applying a standard library.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves 6 distinct steps: structure building, DFT relaxations, initial dimer run, GPR training, iterative GPR-dimer loop, and final barrier computation. It requires coordinating GPAW (DFT), GPyTorch (ML), and custom logic across several scripts, along with I/O and convergence handling. This is a moderate multi-stage orchestration, not a single script.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a custom GPR-accelerated dimer method for solid-state diffusion, combining multi-task GPR with an inverse-distance kernel, DFT relaxations, and an iterative feedback loop. The conceptual difficulty is high due to the non-trivial integration of machine learning and materials theory, while execution involves a multi-stage pipeline with several external libraries. Computational resources are modest (CPU-only DFT on small supercells).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The paper used CPU-only DFT (VASP/GPAW) on 54-atom and 48-atom supercells, requiring ~20-23 core-hours on 64-core AMD EPYC. GPR training is lightweight. Memory needs are a few GB for DFT; no large external datasets.
